mcq.q: Look at his muddy boots. He ___ playing football.
___ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
By the time we got to the cinema, the film ___.
You can borrow my camera as long as you ___ careful with it.
The last minutes were so exciting that we were on the ___ of our seats.
I'll buy the phone if you ___ a free case.
After weighing ___ the pros and cons, she chose the online course.
Which sentence balances an argument best?
options: It's cheap, so I bought it.
On the one hand, it's cheap; on the other hand, it's slow.
I want it because it's cheap.
It's cheap and fast and good.

mcq.q: Your friend offers 50 riyals for a game you're selling for 80. What's the best way to compromise?
Which is the best way to speculate about a photo?
options: It looks as though they've just won something.

listen.script: Look at this picture. The man is soaked, and he's holding a broken umbrella. It must have been raining really hard, and judging by his face, he isn't very happy about it.
listen.q: What does the speaker think happened?
options: The man had lost his umbrella.
The man had just won a prize.

listen.script: Moving to the city has its advantages. There are better schools and more things to do. On the other hand, the traffic is terrible and the houses are much more expensive. On balance, I'd still rather stay in the village.
options: To move to a new country.

listen.script: OK, I'll let you have your friends over this weekend, provided that you tidy up afterwards and everyone has gone home before eleven. If not, that's the last time.
listen.q: What is one condition the parent sets?
options: Make sure the friends leave before eleven.

listen.script: We had just put up our tents when, out of nowhere, a sandstorm hit the camp. By the time it stopped, half our things had blown away. Eventually, we found most of them behind a dune.
options: Before they arrived at the camp.
Right after they had put up their tents.
After they had found their things.

read.passage: Last spring, my class went to AlUla on a three-day school trip. On the one hand, I was excited to see the ancient tombs at Hegra; on the other hand, I was worried about the long bus journey. As it turned out, the journey was the best part. We had just left Madinah when our guide started telling stories about the Nabataeans, who had carved the tombs about two thousand years earlier. By the time we arrived, everyone was desperate to explore. Although it was hot, we walked for hours. On the last day, our teacher let us choose between a balloon ride and a night-sky tour, as long as we all agreed. Eventually, we reached a compromise: the balloon ride at sunrise and stargazing after dinner.

qs.q: What was the writer worried about before the trip?
When did the guide start telling stories?
What condition did the teacher set for the last day?
options: The students had to pay extra.

qs.q: What did the class finally decide?
options: To do only the balloon ride

aloud: Judging by the expressions on their faces, they must have just heard some good news.
Although tourism boosts the economy, too many visitors can cause damage to ancient sites.

speak: Look around the room you are in. What do you think happened here earlier today? Use 'must have' and 'might have'.
